abstract: Previous research on recommender systems has primarily focused on the short-term effects of recommendations on customer search and purchase behaviors. This study investigates the effect of a recommender system on customer loyalty and long-run retail sales using a randomized field experiment. We manipulated the presence vs. absence of product recommendations from an item-based collaborative filtering recommender system at an online retailer. The results reveal that displaying recommendations increases consumers’ purchases of recommended products, but at the cost of reduced sales of non-recommended products, potentially failing to increase total sales in the short run. Nevertheless, consumers’ shift of focus (to recommended products) due to the presence of recommendations plays an important role in enhancing customer loyalty. When recommendations are disabled, our findings suggest that long-term sales decrease significantly due to reduced customer loyalty. The results show that the loyalty effect is primarily driven by a preference effect, in which displaying recommendations induces consumers to view more recommended products, enhancing their shopping experience and increasing repeat visits. For returning customers, who may consider product recommendations a necessary element of a desirable shopping experience, a one-time disablement of recommendations can directly lead to defection. The findings provide insights into the true value of recommender systems.

ob.ai_reason: 推荐系统（协同过滤）为AI核心变量
ob.tldr: 基于在线零售商的随机田野实验，探究协同过滤推荐系统对消费者忠诚度与长期销售的影响。短期内推荐系统虽增加推荐品销量、减少非推荐品销量，总销量未必提升，但通过'偏好效应'引导消费者聚焦推荐品，提升购物体验与回访频率，从而增强客户忠诚度。推荐一旦关闭，忠诚客户流失导致长期销售显著下降，揭示了推荐系统的长期战略价值。

title: How Do Recommender Systems Benefit Online Retailers in the Long Run? Evidence from a Field Experiment1
title_zh: 推荐系统如何长期惠及在线零售商？来自一项实地实验的证据
